newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran hopes to sign South Pars gas deal in month.
newsitem.headline: Iran hopes to sign South Pars gas deal in month.

text.p: Iran on Saturday said it expected soon to make an award for the second phase of its huge South Pars gasfield.
"I am sure that for the South Pars we will make an announcement in one month, Mohammad Nejadhosseinian, Deputy Minister of Intenational Affairs at Iran's oil ministry, said.
He said French oil company Total, tipped by industry sources as frontrunner for the contract, was a candidate for the $2 billion to $3 billion contract in Iran's Gulf waters.
"Maybe Total...but Shell is also active," he said.
Total vice president Christophe de Margerie said his company was keen to secure the deal under the right conditions.
"What we would like to do is finalise as soon as possible," he said of the negotiations with state National Iranian Oil Corp (NIOC).

Total is already developing Iran's offshore Sirri A and E oilfields, becoming Iran's first foreign investor since the Iranian revolution nearly 20 years ago. The company has maintained close ties with Iran despite U.S. sanctions aimed at punishing foreign companies that deal with the country.

The Iran-Libya Sanctions bill aims to prevent foreign companies investing more than $40 million in Iran but has been challenged by the European Union, which hopes the United States will water down its conditions.
Royal Dutch/Shell remains in the race for South Pars but appears unlikely to sign any contract before a resolution of the row.
"We are still very interested in South Pars," Shell's exploration director A. J. Parsley said on Friday.
